data.title: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) — oral + topical

data.category: More from Khopkar · Vitamins & trace elements
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Vitamins & trace elements_

**Class:** Water-soluble antioxidant vitamin

## Mechanism of action
- Cofactor for prolyl and lysyl hydroxylase (collagen synthesis)
- Antioxidant (neutralises UV-generated free radicals); inhibits tyrosinase (depigmenting); regenerates vitamin E

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Scurvy: perifollicular haemorrhage, corkscrew hairs, gum bleeding, poor wound healing, woody oedema
- Adjunct in wound healing, iron absorption (with iron), Ehlers–Danlos (limited)
- Topical L-ascorbic acid 10–20% (pH <3.5) or stable derivatives (magnesium ascorbyl phosphate): photoageing, melasma and PIH (adjunct), photoprotection booster (with vitamin E and ferulic acid)

## Dose & formulations
- Scurvy: 300–1000 mg/day for 1 month; supplement 500 mg/day
- Topical: once daily in the morning under sunscreen

## Adverse effects
- Oral high doses: GI upset, oxalate kidney stones, haemolysis in G6PD deficiency (IV)
- Topical: stinging, yellow staining as it oxidises (unstable in air/light)

## Contraindications
- Recurrent oxalate stones (high dose); haemochromatosis

## Drug interactions
- Increases iron absorption; may interfere with glucose meters (IV)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe.

## Viva points
- Scurvy: corkscrew hairs and perifollicular haemorrhage
- Topical vitamin C — antioxidant; must be acidic and fresh

_Sources: Khopkar (Ascorbic acid; topical vitamin C); Wolverton 4e ch.57. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
